title: BTC to XMR Swap Completed but Monero Is Not Showing: Wallet Sync, Confirmations, and Locked Balance

friendlyUrls.anchor: Wallet recovery after an app closes

keyQuestions: Why is the swap Completed while XMR is still absent?
How long until XMR is spendable?
Why can I see the incoming transaction but not use the amount?
Can I confirm my Monero balance by pasting the address into an explorer?
What does a wrong restore height look like?
Can support synchronize the wallet for me?
quickSteps: Capture the order number, payout TXID, amount, destination, and status time in a private note.
Locate the payout hash and determine whether it is waiting for a block or already mined.
Open the wallet and account that generated the destination, then let its scan pass the payout block.
Read total and available balances separately, allowing 10 confirmations when the output is visible but locked.
Request official support only when the checkpoints conflict, and provide case details without wallet-access secrets.

issueRouting.start: The BTC to XMR order is Completed, but the Monero wallet does not show a spendable payout.

branches.if: The order has no XMR payout TXID.
then: Do not change wallet settings before a payout reference exists.

branches.if: The payout is mined, but the wallet has not scanned past its block.
then: Open the wallet and account that generated the destination.
Use a reliable node and let synchronization continue.
Wait until the wallet scan height passes the payout block.

branches.if: The payout is visible, but the available balance remains lower.
then: Allow the output to reach 10 confirmations.
Do not rescan or send a second payment.

riskNotes: A Completed order status does not prove that the receiving wallet has scanned the payout block.
A synchronized application can still show zero when the wrong wallet or account is open.
A restore height set after the payout block can omit the incoming transaction.
Sending a second BTC payment creates another timeline and makes the original case harder to diagnose.
Recovery words, private keys, wallet files, passwords, and remote access are never required for support diagnostics.
